## About this dataset

There are six eddy covariance towers that make continuous measurements of regional hydrology and carbon balance in the region. This long-term eddy covariance tower network includes 2008-ongoing data collection in a freshwater marl prairie (TS/Ph-1; US-Esm) and a freshwater marsh (SRS-2; US-Elm), 2016-2021 data collection from a mangrove scrub (TS/Ph-7; US-TaS), 2004-2023 data collection from a tall mangrove forest (SRS-6; US-Skr), 2020-ongoing data collection from a tower at the ecotone of marl prairie and mangrove scrub (SE1; US-EvM), and 2018-ongoing data collection from an aquatic Tower in Florida Bay (Bob Allen Key; US-FBE). This data package is an inventory of eddy covariance tower data and metadata available through the AmeriFlux repository. This package also contains environmental and meteorological variables measured at the SRS-6 mangrove forest using an eddy covariance flux tower in the southeastern Florida Coastal Everglades from 2004 to 2023.

`sitename` · `latitude` · `longitude` · `start_datetime` · `end_datetime` · `site_info_URL` · `publication_DOI` · `repository_URL` · `TIMESTAMP` · `SUp_Avg` · `SDn_Avg` · `LUp_Avg` · `RlNet_Avg` · `BP_mbar_Avg` · `RH1_Avg` · `Tair1_Avg` · `ST1_Avg` · `Rain_1_Tot` · `Salinity`

_Units, definitions and uncertainty are documented in the archived metadata (EML)._

## Research applications [needs review]{.badge .text-bg-warning}

- Finding long-term CO2 and CH4 flux records for subtropical wetlands and mangroves
- Blue carbon and coastal greenhouse-gas budgets

## Known limitations

- Flux records themselves are served by AmeriFlux; this package is an inventory plus SRS-6 auxiliary data

## Get the data with code

::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# install.packages("EDIutils")
library(EDIutils)

pkg <- "knb-lter-fce.1245.4"
entities <- read_data_entity_names(pkg)   # list the files in the package
entities

# read the first entity into R
raw <- read_data_entity(pkg, entities$entityId[1])
dat <- readr::read_csv(raw)
```

### Python

```python
import io, requests, pandas as pd

pkg = "knb-lter-fce/1245/4"
base = "https://pasta.lternet.edu/package"
ids = requests.get(f"{base}/data/eml/{pkg}").text.split()
names = requests.get(f"{base}/name/eml/{pkg}").text
print(names)

csv = requests.get(ids[0]).content
df = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(csv))
```
